title: LCTMwalk: GPU-Accelerated Transient Thermal Simulation for Liquid-Cooled 2.5D/3D ICs via Random Walks on Circuit Networks of Modified Compact Thermal Models
problem: Existing matrix-solving acceleration methods for compact thermal models (CTMs) are inadequate for high-speed iterative transient thermal analysis of large-scale liquid-cooled 2.5D/3D ICs, and random walk methods were not applicable to liquid-cooled CTM circuits.
motivation: Thermal management is critical in 2.5D/3D IC design; liquid cooling requires fast thermal simulation during iterative design optimization.
method: LCTMwalk proposes a novel GPU-accelerated random walk method by: (1) replacing voltage-controlled current source with diode model to enable random walks on liquid-cooled CTM circuits, (2) improving transient analysis with time-backward random walk and time-domain path reuse for local node solutions.
key_novelty: Adaptation of random walk method to liquid-cooled CTM circuits via diode model replacement, enabling GPU acceleration for large-scale transient thermal analysis.
contributions: Diode model replacement enabling random walks on liquid-cooled CTM-derived circuit networks
Time-backward random walk with time-domain path reuse for transient analysis
GPU acceleration scaling to million-scale thermal problems
14-22× speedup versus ADI method with high accuracy (<1 K error)

metrics.speedup: 14-22× speedup versus state-of-the-art ADI GPU method
metrics.accuracy: <1 K temperature error compared to 3D-ICE simulator

limitations: Evaluation on specific 2.5D/3D IC configurations; applicability to other thermal simulation domains not explored.
